package.welcome_message: Land in Amman, then 2 exploring days through Balqa (2 days).

trip.title: Balqa Explorer
trip.summary: Arrival, then Balqa (2 days). Walk outdoors in the morning. Keep the afternoon for shade, meals, or indoor visits.

planning.strategy: You land at 18:11, so arrival night stays in Amman — hotel, a meal, rest. The touring days start the next morning. After that the days stay on a short loop: Balqa (2 days). It's a hot month, so the outdoor sites go before midday.
assumptions: Travel times between cities are estimated qualitatively, not as exact minutes, unless evidence exists.
Opening hours are used only when present on the catalog record.

climate.typical_pattern: High daytime heat, especially in the Jordan Valley and desert.
climate.outdoor_guidance: Walk outdoors in the morning. Keep the afternoon for shade, meals, or indoor visits.

decisions.title: Each exploring day stays in one area
decisions.why: Mixing far-apart cities in one day makes the trip exhausting.
decisions.effect: After arrival, the days run Balqa (2 days).

decisions.title: A route from what you like
decisions.why: No cities were named, so the days follow the places that matched religious sites, museums, and shopping.
decisions.effect: Those retrieved areas become the route: Balqa (2 days).

decisions.title: This trip stays in one part of Jordan
decisions.why: 2 exploring days is too short for both the north and the south.
decisions.effect: So this journey focuses on the north and center, and those places get proper time.

decisions.title: Night one is near the airport
decisions.effect: Sleep in Amman on arrival night. The exploring days start the next morning.

decisions.title: Settle in this evening
decisions.effect: Food and rest first. A nearby stop only if enough evening remains, then back to the hotel.

decisions.title: Then you move closer to the places you came for
decisions.why: Sleeping in the same city you visit beats a long commute every morning.
decisions.effect: After the arrival night, nearby days share one hotel. You only move when the next area is too far for a day trip.

decisions.title: Mornings for the outdoors
decisions.why: High daytime heat, especially in the Jordan Valley and desert.
decisions.effect: Walk heritage and nature in the morning. Save museums, meals, and shade for the afternoon.

decisions.title: A relaxed pace
decisions.effect: On exploring days, plan on about 3 visits and 3 meals. Arrival follows the time left after food and rest.

decisions.title: Planned with children in mind
decisions.effect: Family-friendly stops come first, and long stacked hikes are avoided.

decisions.title: 4 star stays
decisions.effect: Hotels are taken from listings at that star level when the city has them. If it does not, we use the closest listed tier and say so.

decisions.title: A comfort budget
decisions.effect: We lean toward more comfortable stays and dining when those places exist.

decisions.title: Chosen around what you care about
decisions.effect: Stops follow religious sites, museums, and shopping. Unrelated places stay off the list.

days.summary: Afternoon/evening arrival in Amman: eat and rest first. A quiet first evening.

schedule.name: Dardasha Kitchen
schedule.description: A cozy neighborhood spot offering comforting Levantine home-style dishes, fresh daily specials, and warm hospitality.
schedule.reason: Dinner near the hotel. Nothing more tonight.

schedule.name: Amman Rotana
schedule.description: Jordan's tallest building at 188 metres, this five-star Abdali tower hotel holds 412 rooms and suites across 50 floors, with several restaurants, a seasonal outdoor pool, a 24-hour gym and a full-service spa.
schedule.reason: Check in and rest first. Add a nearby stop only if enough evening is left. 5-star stay, as requested

days.transport_notes: You land at 18:11. The drive from Queen Alia to Amman is about 45 minutes. Times below start after that transfer.
